title: enqueue of an existing job id with a DIFFERENT tenant (or payload) returns ok 'exists': tenant B's job is silently never queued, and B can probe whether tenant A holds an id
area: packages/core/src/job-queue/file-job-queue.ts:49 (if (s.jobs.some(j => j.id === input.id)) return ok 'exists') and queue-types.ts JobQueue.enqueue doc
evidence: Checker model property (1,000 seeds): 4,741 enqueues hit an existing id with a different tenant and 2,376 with a different payload; every one returned {ok:true,value:'exists'} and stored nothing. Repro: q.enqueue({id:'j1',tenantId:'ta',payload:1}) -> 'enqueued'; q.enqueue({id:'j1',tenantId:'tb',payload:2}) -> {ok:true,value:'exists'}; tenant tb never has a job and is told it is queued. The stored job is untouched (no overwrite, no tenant move), so the defect is the success report, not corruption.
fix_direction: Treat the tenant as part of the identity: if the stored job's tenantId differs, return a typed error (e.g. code 'id-conflict') and do not confirm; for a same-tenant different-payload re-enqueue return a distinguishable result (e.g. error 'payload-mismatch'); keep 'exists' for identical repeats. Alternative: key by (tenantId,id). Add both to the contract tests.
class: tenancy + lost job (reported success for a job that was not queued)

title: Lost update between the pre-rename re-read and the rename (cross-process or thread); every operation is a full read + full rewrite with no pruning
evidence: Real-fs test with an fs wrapper running a second FileJobQueue.enqueue on the same dir at each fs call of the first instance's enqueue: hooks at read/mkdirp/create/re-read give 'conflict' with nothing lost; a hook exactly at rename loses the other instance's job (stored only fromA, A reports enqueued). Unreachable in one synchronous thread, reachable with a second process or worker thread. Growth (real fs, 99% done jobs): 100 jobs 30 KB enqueue 28 ms / claim 30 ms; 1,000 jobs 270 KB 57/49 ms; 5,000 jobs 1.3 MB 68/59 ms.
fix_direction: Before any second writer exists: add a lock (meeting-bot join-rules store style) or version-based CAS, and prune/archive done and dead jobs. Not a defect while strictly single process.
class: data write, deferred by documented scope
